text:
marta: saw a weird latency hump after the INT8-kv rollout at 11:32 PT. 95p up ~40ms, mem down ~120MB, decode qual noise on long contexts
ashok: repro'd locally on a small rig, seems tied to mixed-precision kernel switch when kv pages hit a certain density
marta: exact numbers?
perf-bot: profile summary attached: decode_threads=8, batch=4->3, avg_latency=56ms->98ms, 95p=78ms->118ms, kv_mem=1.9GB->1.78GB
zofia: looks like "kv-page-compaction" heuristic flipped mid-run, causing a different kernel path (fp8 fallback) for >64k entries
devin: hmm we didn't change compaction rules in the rollout. what's the kernel selection rule code path?
ashok: small snippet from runtime logs: 

```
kernel_selector: choose_fastest_for(seq_len, batch_size, kv_density)
kv_density=0.63 -> selected kernel=quantized_int8_unpack_v2
kv_density=0.71 -> selected kernel=mixed_fp8_fallback
```

marta: so density threshold oscillates around 0.7 and combined with batching hysteresis we get route flips mid-batch
devin: that matches the spike timing -> when request mix changes, kernel swap inserts a micro-jit and pagewalks spike
zofia: calibration/scale mismatch can amplify decode noise when switching back/forth
ashok: repro steps I used:
```
# reproduce locally
export RUNTIME_KV_PAGES=2048
export RUNTIME_KV_QUANT_MODE=int8
./run_decode_bench --model=redwood-3b --batch=3 --seq=1024 --rps=1200 --mix=long_context
```
output: "steady 95p=76ms" then after ~20s: "95p=126ms, p99=260ms"
marta: interestingly memory drops slightly when fallback happens — pages re-encode to fp8 packed layout then decompress when served
perf-bot: heap snapshot diff: kv_pages_active=2048->2016, cached_prefixes=1240->1176, net_mem=-124MB
devin: two hypotheses: (1) kernel swap costs + cache eviction churn, (2) quantization calibration edge-case creating extra decode iterations
zofia: I think calibration is part but not full story. we saw consistent small token churn (0.1-0.6%) when toggling kernels locally
nashok: quick experiment results: turning OFF kernel hysteresis (force sticky kernel for 5s) -> 95p stable, avg latency negligible change
marta: ok that points at switching overhead rather than a pure quality regression
devin: can we add a temporary hysteresis knob into prod to confirm? set to 3s and watch 95p for next hour
zofia: adding rollout patch: 
```
runtime.config.kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms=3000
runtime.config.kv_density_threshold_override=0.75
```
marta: rolling to canary now (canary=13% traffic). will watch p95, p99, and decode logits divergence on eval prompts
perf-bot: canary deployment complete. monitoring hook: p95 latency, kv_mem, decode-bleu-diff
ashok: FYI I pushed a small tweak to quant calib path to skip re-calib for pages with <8 updates/sec — cut churn in half in my bench
devin: nice. if hysteresis stabilizes we can schedule a follow-up to evaluate removing the density flip entirely and prefer kernel A for long contexts
zofia: also add logging for "kernel_switch_reason" and include kv_density in request trace — will help root cause
marta: thanks all. outcome plan: 1) keep hysteresis 3s on canary 2) add kernel switch logs and calib skip 3) run long-run decode eval against golden prompts 4) if stable, promote and then open a perf playbook note
ashok: adding short note to incident playbook: "kv ghosting" shorthand for this behavior + quick mitigations
marta: perfect. will post update in #incidents if we see regressions. closing thread unless new alerts pop up.
